messages:
jordan: Heads up — spotted a weird class of funcall parse failures in the pegasus-v2q int4 canary. ~2% of requests with long metadata arrays are coming back with truncated JSON (missing trailing brace) and failing schema validation.

lia: Ugh. Is that correlated with sequence length / batch packing? :eyes:

jordan: Looks like it spikes when total tokens ~> 480 and we hit a tail clip in the quant runtime. Repro locally when forcing short kvcache margin. Logs show final tokens cut mid-utf8 and then stream ended.

oscar: Do you have a dump? small snippet would help.

jordan: Paste of the truncated suffix (redacted ids):
```
... , "metadata": ["sensor_reading_123", "…", "47





```
Notice last field ends without closing quotes/bracket.

maya: I ran mirror-replay on a sample of 5k requests — quant variant (int4) has 1.9% funcall_parse_failures vs 0.1% for float32 baseline. Memory/latency win still material, but correctness regression unacceptable for canary.

sam: Is this an encoder or runtime tokenization mismatch? Could be our token merger that tries to pack multiple requests into batch leading to boundary split.

jordan: Two hypotheses: (1) kernel quant tail clipping when buffer limit reached (clip/drop last bytes) and (2) streaming flush earlier than token commit under small batch. Both would produce partial utf8/JSON suffix.

caro: Quick mitigation: add a post-stream sanity check that validates last 64 bytes for valid UTF-8 and JSON-terminating chars; if invalid, append sentinel "\n\n<TRUNC_GUARD>\n\n" and mark request for async-rescue. That buys us time while we debug runtime.

lia: We already have a JSON-repair heuristic used by some toolcall adapters (attempts to close braces, fix quotes). We could enable it for quant canaries only and emit telemetry. Risk: may mask real logical truncation where arguments are actually incomplete.

oscar: Agreed. We should not auto-repair for fields that are required by schema (e.g., signature/intent). But for optional metadata arrays, repair is acceptable. Can we gate by schema path?

jordan: Yes — plan: 1) pause global rollout of pegasus-v2q int4 canary, 2) enable conservative repair for optional leaf arrays only, 3) bump kvcache margin + holdback packing when seq_len > 420, 4) run 100k sample A/B with mirror traffic (mirror to int4 + baseline) and collect parse_failures_by_schema_path.

maya: Telemetry needed: funcall_parse_failures, parse_repair_applied, repaired_fields (list), latency delta for repaired path. Also capture sample tokens around boundary for offline kernel debugging.

sam: I'll add a short-lived flag to runtime: quant_tail_guard=true which pads outputs with a reserved sentinel token at the end of generation so we can detect/avoid mid-byte drops. Low-risk toggle.

caro: +1. Also add a canary alert: if parse failures > 0.5% for 1 minute, auto-fail the canary and revert to float baseline.

deploy-bot: deploy request received: enable quant_tail_guard on pegasus-v2q-canary. Expect rolling update across 6 nodes.

lia: One more ask: add a lightweight unit test in runtime that simulates partial-last-byte truncation after detokenize and verify that JSON-repair heuristics don't invent required fields (fail if required missing).

jordan: Good call. I'll draft the test and run the A/B. Putting an action list: 
- jordan: draft test + run 100k mirror (ETA today EOD)
- sam: add quant_tail_guard flag + kvcache margin holdback (ETA 4h)
- caro: telemetry alert + metrics (ETA 2h)
- lia: enable conservative repair for optional arrays (ETA 3h)
- maya: pause rollout and collect baseline snapshots (done)

maya: Thanks. If A/B shows <0.2% residual parse failures with repair+guard, we can consider re-enabling gradual rollout. If not, revert to float32 for now. :thumbsup:

oscar: Ping me when you have the token dumps — I want to instrument kernel to see where bytes are lost.

jordan: Will drop sample file in /infra/benchmarks/pegasus-v2q/trace-7390012345.log (redacted).

caro: Filing a short postmortem-lite ticket and linking this thread. cc @eng-sre for canary rollback runbook.

sam: Nice triage. Appreciate the quick mitigation plan.

jordan: closing loop — will post results in this thread once A/B finishes.
